page.text:
A function is the mathematical embodiment of a rule that assigns to each
input exactly one output. Having built sets and their Cartesian products,
we can now say precisely what a function is: a way of associating with
every element of one set a unique element of another. Functions, and the
binary operations that are a special case of them, are the tools with
which the algebraic structures of the next chapter are described.
